source: Chen, Lin, Schaerli, Zhou (2023/2024) Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug
finding: Model runs its code, explains it line by line (rubber duck), reads the execution result, then revises. Execution feedback matters most; explanation alone gives small gains.
numbers: Table 2, MBPP: GPT-4 baseline 72.8, simple feedback 78.8, unit-test feedback 80.4, UT+explanation 80.6, UT+trace 80.2. TransCoder GPT-4: 77.3 to 90.4 with UT. Codex Spider dev: 81.3 to 84.1 with explanation (no tests).
limits: Few-shot; MBPP shows only a subset of tests; gains are against one-shot baselines. On Spider GPT-4 gain was only 73.2 to 73.6.
agent_relevance: S5 REVISE: revision should be driven by real execution output. Explaining the code is a minor add-on, not a locator.

source: Chen, Lin, Schaerli, Zhou (2023/2024) Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug (no-execution ablation)
finding: Remove unit-test execution and self-debugging nearly vanishes or turns negative for some models: models are overconfident in their own first answer.
numbers: Table 3 MBPP no execution: Codex 61.4 to 57.6 (simple), 64.4 (expl), 66.2 (trace). GPT-4 72.8 to 76.0 simple, 76.4 trace. TransCoder GPT-4 77.3 to 78.4 at best; GPT-3.5 unchanged at 89.1.
limits: Same few benchmarks. Trace feedback is the most consistent self-generated aid.
agent_relevance: Supports G2: no revision from the model's opinion alone. Without a real failing output, S5 should not fire.

source: Chen, Lin, Schaerli, Zhou (2023/2024) Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug (sample efficiency)
finding: One debug round on a greedy sample matches many extra samples. Later rounds add almost nothing.
numbers: Spider: debugging a greedy output matches baseline with 16 samples; debugging from 8 samples beats baseline with 32. Gain after the first debug turn is within 0.1%. Abstract: 9% gain on hardest Spider level.
limits: Spider is SQL, not general programs.
agent_relevance: Cap S5 at one to two rounds (matches the schema). Debugging is cheaper than resampling when an execution check exists.

source: Olausson, Inala, Wang, Gao, Solar-Lezama (2024) Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
finding: At equal compute, self-repair often does not beat drawing more independent samples. The bottleneck is the model's own feedback (diagnosis) on its code, not the fix step.
numbers: GPT-4 on APPS: 10 samples + 1 repair each (about 20 total) gives 1.05x pass@20; 2 samples + 10 repairs each (22 total) gives 0.97x pass@22. Replacing GPT-4's own explanation with a human programmer's raised the repaired-and-passing fraction from 33.3% to 52.6% (1.58x). Stronger-model feedback also lifted weaker models above both baselines.
limits: Python, HumanEval and APPS, self-contained tasks; human study small. Full test suite given (no public/private split).
agent_relevance: Direct machine evidence for locate-first: diagnosis quality is the limit. Spend budget on diverse first attempts plus a good located diagnosis, not many blind repair rounds.

source: Huang, Chen, Mishra et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without an oracle label, asking the model to review and fix its own answer lowers accuracy. Earlier gains came from stopping when the answer was already right.
numbers: Table 2 (oracle): GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 89.7, HotpotQA 26.0 to 29.0; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5, HotpotQA 49 to 59. Table 3 (intrinsic): GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9, 75.1, 74.7 over rounds; CSQA 75.8 to 38.1 to 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0, HotpotQA 49 to 43. 74.7% of GSM8K answers stayed unchanged for GPT-3.5.
limits: Reasoning tasks, not code with a test runner. Prompts were criticised as weak. Two rounds only.
agent_relevance: Core support for G2 and G1: self-revision with no real signal is harmful. Keep revision gated on a located failing output.

source: Tyen, Mansoor, Carbune, Chen, Mak (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: Finding the first wrong step is hard for models; fixing it once told where is easy. Locate and fix are separate skills, as in Vessey's phases.
numbers: BIG-Bench Mistake (2186 CoT traces, 5 tasks). Best mistake-finding: GPT-4 52.87 overall with direct step-level prompting. Backtracking from the true location lifts originally wrong answers by +18 to +44 points (e.g. multistep arithmetic +43.92, Dyck +36.86), at a cost of -0 to -11 on originally correct ones; random locations give smaller gains (+5 to +21) and larger losses (to -16).
limits: Synthetic algorithmic tasks, small test sets; a trained classifier for location is needed in practice.
agent_relevance: Strongest single result for locate before fix: give the fixer the located failing step from code, never ask the model to find it by judgment.

source: Kamoi, Zhang, Zhang, Han, Zhang (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
finding: Survey: no major work shows successful self-correction by prompting alone under fair settings on general tasks. Positive results use oracle information, weak initial prompts, or external feedback such as tools and code execution.
numbers: Table 4 audits prior studies for oracle use or weak baselines (RCI, Reflexion, others). Exception: tasks where checking is easier than generating, such as decomposable multi-answer tasks (CoVe).
limits: Literature review, not new experiments.
agent_relevance: Justifies a verifier-in-the-loop revise step; self-critique is allowed only where the check is cheaper than the generation.

source: Shinn, Cassano, Berman, Gopinath, Narasimhan, Yao (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Agent writes unit tests, runs them, reflects in words on failures, retries with the reflection in memory. Big gain on HumanEval, a loss on MBPP-Python because of weak self-written tests.
numbers: Pass@1: HumanEval-Python GPT-4 80.1 to Reflexion 91.0; HumanEval-Rust 60.0 to 68.0; MBPP-Python 80.1 to 77.1 (worse); MBPP-Rust 70.9 to 75.4; LeetcodeHard-Python 7.5 to 15.0. False-positive rate (tests pass, code wrong): 1.4% HumanEval-Py vs 16.3% MBPP-Py.
limits: The test suite is model-written, so a pass can be false. Authors state false positives are the dangerous case.
agent_relevance: Matches G3: a pass counts only on a check the answer was not fitted to. Self-made tests need a held-out or mutated check.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
finding: Generate, self-critique, refine loop. Large gains on style-like tasks, none on math reasoning where correctness needs outside checking.
numbers: Table 1 with GPT-3.5: Math reasoning 64.1 to 64.1 (0 gain); sentiment reversal 8.8 to 30.4; acronym generation 41.6 to 56.4; constrained generation 28.0 to 37.0.
limits: Most gains are judged by human or model preference on subjective tasks; the table was garbled in text extraction so code-task cells are not quoted.
agent_relevance: Self-feedback helps taste tasks, not correctness; do not use it as the locate step.

source: Yang, Jimenez, Wettig et al. (2024) SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
finding: Tool design for the agent changes debugging results as much as the model. Trajectories start with reproduce or localise, then edit, then rerun. Linting at edit time blocks cascading errors.
numbers: GPT-4 Turbo resolves 12.47% of 2,294 SWE-bench tasks. Lite ablations: search tool Summarized 18.0 vs No search 15.7 vs Iterative 12.0; edit with linting 18.0 vs without 15.0 vs no edit tool 10.3. The create-edit-python pattern appears 156 times in turns 1 to 3.
limits: Ablations on a 300-task Lite subset; one main model. Iterative search made agents look at every hit and hurt results.
agent_relevance: Agents already follow reproduce, then localise, then edit. Show compact summarised localisation output; check edits at once (cheap guard before S4).

source: Xia, Deng, Dunn, Zhang (2024) Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
finding: A fixed three-step pipeline (localise hierarchically, repair with several samples, validate by tests) with no agent loop beat open-source agents on SWE-bench Lite at low cost. Hierarchical file, then function, then line localisation keeps context small.
numbers: 32.00% resolved (96 of 300) at $0.70 per issue. Going straight from file level to edit lines was worse in cost and score. Correct-location rate tracks solve rate; one commercial tool had 90.0% file-level location but only 23.67% solved.
limits: Authors flag 4.3% of Lite problems with exact-patch leaks and 10.0% with missing info. Location match is only an approximation of repair success.
agent_relevance: Supports a code-driven locate step before S5, narrowing in stages. Localise by code and retrieval, ask the model for the fix only.

source: Zhong, Wang, Shang (2024) Debug like a Human: LDB, LLM Debugger via Verifying Runtime Execution Step by Step
finding: Gives the model real variable values after each basic block; the model judges each block right or wrong. Beats self-debug by explanation or imagined trace.
numbers: Pass@1 HumanEval GPT-3.5 73.8 baseline, Self-Debug expl +7.3 (81.1), LDB 82.9 (+9.1). With GPT-4 seed 87.2: SD +1.2, LDB +2.4. Reflexion seed 91.5: SD +0.6, LDB 95.1 (+3.6). StarCoder HumanEval: SD -0.6 to 0.0, LDB +0.6.
limits: Visible tests only; gains up to 9.8 points; shrinks as seed quality rises.
agent_relevance: Real runtime state beats imagined state. A code-run tracer feeding S5 is the machine version of a breakpoint.

source: Yuan, Moss, El Feghali et al. (2025) debug-gym: A Text-Based Environment for Interactive Debugging
finding: Giving agents a Python debugger (pdb) helps strong models on real repo bugs but hurts weak ones when given from the start; adding pdb only after 5 failed rewrites works best.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite success, Claude 3.7 Sonnet: rewrite 37.2, debug 48.4, debug(5) 52.1. Text: weaker models (GPT-4o, 4o-mini, Llama-3.3-70B) lose with early pdb; o1-preview, o3-mini and Claude gain; debug(5) beats rewrite for every model. On short Aider tasks pdb made no clear difference (o3-mini 95.2 rewrite vs 94.2 debug).
limits: Table cells for non-Claude models were garbled in extraction; only the Claude row and the text claims are used. Three runs each.
agent_relevance: Debugger tools should unlock after the cheap rewrite route fails (an impasse), not at the start. Fits G1: act on a signal.

source: Bouzenia, Devanbu, Pradel (2025) RepairAgent: An Autonomous, LLM-Based Agent for Program Repair
finding: Agent with a state flow (gather information, collect repair ingredients, validate) and tools to state and discard hypotheses. Fixed 164 Defects4J bugs. Realistic localisation costs a lot against perfect localisation.
numbers: 164 bugs fixed (74 in Defects4J v1.2, 90 in v2.0). With GZoltar spectrum localisation instead of perfect localisation: 16 bugs fixed for $29, a 25% drop in fixes and 81% rise in cost (as stated in the paper).
limits: Java; perfect localisation is an upper bound not met in real use. Read by text search, not every section.
agent_relevance: Quantifies how much repair success is localisation. A hypothesis-state tool is an existing LLM-loop version of Vessey-style strategy.

source: Kang, An, Yoo (2024) A Quantitative and Qualitative Evaluation of LLM-Based Explainable Fault Localization (AutoFL)
finding: Model navigates the repo with function calls (covered classes, method bodies, failing test) to find the faulty method and explain it. Beats spectrum-based localisation (Ochiai).
numbers: 798 real bugs. Method-level acc@1 higher than Ochiai by 19.7% on Defects4J and by 166.7% (GPT-3.5) and 233.3% (GPT-4) on BugsInPy. A no-interaction baseline (Test-GPT3.5) is beaten. Paper cites a human study where bug diagnosis took 66% of debugging time (Boehme et al.).
limits: Needs a failing test; GPT-3.5 had trouble digging deep into the repo. Result is relative to a weak SBFL baseline.
agent_relevance: Localisation by interactive tool calls beats one-shot guessing. Repeat runs give a confidence signal.

source: Majgaonkar, Fei, Li, Sarro, Ye (2025) Understanding Code Agent Behaviour: Success and Failure Trajectories
finding: Trajectory study of three agents on SWE-bench. Failed runs are longer and more variable. Agents usually find the right file even when they fail, so wrong file is not the main failure.
numbers: File correct in 72% to 81% of failed trajectories (81% for SWE-agent on Lite). Successful patches hit the right file over 90% of the time. On Verified, 35% to 40% of failures miss the file; on Lite 20% to 25%. Wrong-file runs do not stop sooner.
limits: Three agents with Claude 4 Sonnet; observational, no intervention.
agent_relevance: Locating the file is mostly solved; the open problem is the exact edit and knowing when to stop. Add a length or no-progress stop signal (impasse).

source: Huang, Ye, Sun, Zhang, Zhang, Liu (2026) TraceCoder: Trace-Driven Multi-Agent Debugging of LLM-Generated Code
finding: Three roles: instrument code with probes, analyse the traces for cause, then repair. A rollback keeps only strict improvement; a memory of failed attempts stops repeats.
numbers: Up to 34.43% relative Pass@1 gain (82.00 vs 61.00 second best on one benchmark); 90.72% on another setting vs 81.05% best baseline. Removing the whole iterative repair loop drops 89.04% to 53.77%. Removing instrumentation alone gives a marked decline.
limits: ICSE 2026 paper; baselines vary; tied to Gemini-class models; cost rises.
agent_relevance: Locate by observing real traces before editing; keep best-so-far with rollback (matches S5). Log failed fixes to avoid loops.

source: Adnan and Kuhn (2025) The Debugging Decay Index: Rethinking Debugging Strategies for Code LLMs
finding: Success per debug round falls roughly exponentially; most models lose 60% to 80% of debugging power within 2 to 3 attempts. Clearing context and restarting from the original problem at a computed point recovers some of it.
numbers: 18 models fitted on HumanEval. Fresh start at the DDI threshold: llama3.1:8b 72.56 to 82.82; deepseek-coder-v2:16b 84.1 to 92.1; Mistral-Instruct 54.3 to 62.8. All six models tested for fresh starts improved; token use about equal or lower.
limits: Only HumanEval variants; exponential form fitted to few points; threshold choice unexplored; small local models.
agent_relevance: Evidence for a hard 2-round cap in S5 and a fresh-context restart (S3) after it. Medium confidence: single small study.

source: Tian et al. (2024) DebugBench: Evaluating Debugging Capability of Large Language Models
finding: Runtime feedback helps with syntax and reference errors, where tracebacks name the line, but is unhelpful or harmful for logic errors. Logic bugs and multi-bug programs are harder.
numbers: 4,253 LeetCode-based instances, 4 bug classes; GPT-4-0613 and GPT-3.5 tested with and without runtime feedback; open models score lower than commercial ones. Exact bar values were in figures and not extracted.
limits: No per-cell numbers recorded; first-author attribution from memory.
agent_relevance: A traceback locates only crash-type bugs. For wrong-output bugs S5 needs another located signal (expected versus got, intermediate values).

source: Bo et al. (2025) Who's the Leader? Analyzing Novice Workflows in LLM-Assisted Debugging of Machine Learning Code
finding: Eight novice ML engineers debugged with ChatGPT (4o-mini) while thinking aloud. Two reliance styles: led by the LLM or leading it. Over-reliance on wrong suggestions led into rabbit holes.
numbers: N = 8; task performance correlated with measured ML expertise (Pearson r = .93) but not self-reported expertise.
limits: Formative study, tiny N, one task; skimmed, not read in full.
agent_relevance: Human-AI debugging fails when the human cannot verify. Same for an agent that cannot verify: it needs a check outside the LLM.

source: ICER 2024 Debugging with an AI Tutor: novice help-seeking behaviours and perceptions
finding: 20 introductory students did think-aloud debugging at three points in a semester with a strategy-giving chatbot. Help-seeking varied with familiarity of strategies; students did not see the chatbot as a main way to learn strategies.
numbers: N = 20, three time points (from search summary only).
limits: Qualitative; summary only, page not opened.
agent_relevance: Human learners rarely adopt a strategy a tool suggests; a scaffold must force the order rather than suggest it.

source: Vessey (1985) Expertise in debugging computer programs: A process analysis
finding: Human anchor for this angle: experts used a system-level, breadth-first strategy and kept a model of the whole program; novices went into details. Not re-read this session; background only.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Recalled from background, unopened.
agent_relevance: Machine analogue is locate-before-fix in Agentless and AutoFL; not verified as a causal claim.

source: Shapiro (1983) Algorithmic Program Debugging
finding: Early AI debugger that finds the faulty clause by asking an oracle whether sub-results are right, a divide and conquer on the computation tree. Background only.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Recalled from background, unopened.
agent_relevance: Same shape as LDB block verdicts and Tyen step location: oracle-checked narrowing.

source: Cross-study synthesis of lines c01 to c21 (this agent)
finding: Across studies: (1) real execution output beats imagined output; (2) location by code or tools beats model guess; (3) the fix step is easy once location is right; (4) returns vanish after 1 to 2 rounds; (5) self-written tests give false passes.
numbers: Self-Debug +8 to +12 points with tests; Olausson 1.58x with human diagnosis; Tyen +18 to +44 with true location; DDI loses 60 to 80% of power by round 2 to 3.
limits: Synthesis by this agent, not a new source.
agent_relevance: Basis for S5: code-located failing output, one-line diagnosis, one fix, max 2 rounds, then fresh restart.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (mechanism)
finding: Why self-revision hurts: the model cannot judge its own answer, so it changes right answers to wrong more often than the reverse. On CommonSenseQA plausible wrong options pull it off a correct answer.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA fell from 75.8 to 38.1 after one self-correct round; GPT-4 GSM8K fell 95.5 to 89.0 after two rounds.
limits: Reasoning QA, not debugging with a runner; prompts debated.
agent_relevance: A revise step that can reopen a correct answer needs a code check first; S8 VERIFY and keep best-so-far guard against this.
